title: Left–Right Combinations: Are They Worth More Than Individual Strike Rate for Lucknow Super Giants?
dek: Do left–right batting partnerships unsettle bowlers enough to be worth more than raw strike rate? Lucknow Super Giants' partnerships since 2018 put the theory to a test.
excerpt: Across the rest of the IPL since 2018, left–right pairs have scored no faster than same-handed pairs. For Lucknow Super Giants the gap runs the other way.
author: CricField Editorial Desk
keyTakeaways: LSG scored at {{ev:lr-tmix}} with a left–right pair at the crease and {{ev:lr-tsame}} with a same-handed pair (2018–2026).
For the rest of the league the figures are {{ev:lr-lmix}} and {{ev:lr-lsame}}.
Handedness is known for {{ev:lr-cov}} of deliveries in the window; the rest are excluded.

sections.heading: The Theory of the Awkward Pair
body: Coaches like a left–right partnership because every strike change forces bowlers to reset their line and captains to move fielders. If the theory is right, mixed pairs should score faster than same-handed pairs over a large sample.
CricField tested it by attaching each batter's handedness from player-bio data to every delivery since 2018. Both batters' hands are known for {{ev:lr-cov}} of balls.

sections.heading: What the Partnerships Show
body: Across the rest of the IPL, left–right pairs scored at {{ev:lr-lmix}} runs per over and same-handed pairs at {{ev:lr-lsame}}. For Lucknow Super Giants the figures are {{ev:lr-tmix}} and {{ev:lr-tsame}}.
LSG spent {{ev:lr-tshare}} of their balls since 2018 with a left–right pair at the crease.

sections.heading: Using the Combination Deliberately
body: If a mixed pair is worth even a fraction of a run per over, batting orders can be flexed to keep one left-hander in the middle at all times, especially against finger spin that turns into one hand and away from the other.
The decision is cheap to implement: it changes who walks out next, not who is picked.

sections.heading: Why the Gap Might Be an Illusion
body: Mixed and same-handed pairs do not bat in the same situations. If left-handers are concentrated among openers, mixed pairs will be over-represented in the powerplay, where scoring is easier, and the comparison will flatter them.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: A Tiebreaker, Not a Selection Rule
body: The data does not clearly support the left–right theory league-wide. For Lucknow Super Giants it should decide batting-order ties between batters of similar quality, not override strike rate and survival.
The next step is to repeat the comparison within each phase to remove the powerplay effect.
